BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of the Seller's Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team (Buyer)
**Basis:** Our Buyer Negotiation Playbook, compared against the Seller's "Key Negotiated Positions" and Disclosure Letter. I have treated the Seller's documents as counterparty proposals only.

---

## 1. Overall Read

The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced." Taken together, it would push most of the deal's known risk back onto Wattlebridge:

- **Every claim would be weakened.** Low caps, high excess-only thresholds and short time limits would apply across all claim types.
- **Fraud and title would be swept in.** One "any limitation applies to all Claims" override would cover them too.
- **Every known problem would become unclaimable.** General data-room disclosure plus a blanket buyer-knowledge bar would remove claims for exactly the issues the Disclosure Letter admits are unresolved: Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay and DD-006.

The Seller's labels ("negotiated," "addressed," "agreed price mechanics," "settled," "adequate," "not expected to be material") are assertions, not agreements (playbook §0.4/6.3). In several places the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts the update. For example, it says Bluefen consent and the Riverlark discharge are *not* in hand.

**Staleness point:** the data room and disclosures speak as at 22 September 2026. Today is 4 November 2026. We should require a refreshed disclosure position and current facts before relying on any of this.

---

## 2. Issue-by-Issue Analysis

### A. Liability Regime

**1. General cap: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1)**
- **Departure:** Our position is 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure matches our fallback, but that fallback needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. None has been given.
- **Why it matters:** A matching number does not clear the point. The cap also cannot be judged alone. Paired with these thresholds, time limits and the all-claims override, 20% is worth much less than it looks.
- **Push back:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not signal the fallback.

**2. Thresholds (cl 12.2)**
- **Departure:** The Seller proposes a de minimis of AUD 25,000 (we want AUD 5,000) and a basket of AUD 250,000 recoverable on the excess only (we want AUD 50,000, recoverable from the first dollar).
- **Why it matters:** This is five times our position on both measures, and it moves from a tipping basket to a deductible. Claims under AUD 25k vanish entirely, and the first AUD 250k of loss is permanently absorbed by us.
- **Push back:** Reinstate AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 tipping. Thresholds must not apply to Fundamental claims, specific indemnities, Tax, covenant or payment claims, or fraud.

**3. Time limits (cl 12.3/13)**
- **Departure:** 18 months, against our 24. The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which we do not have.
- **Hidden override:** The Seller also says "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." That extends the general regime silently to Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant claims, and arguably to fraud. It breaches our rule against hidden general-regime overrides.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims. Delete the all-claims override. Instead, each category should carry its own expressly stated regime, with general limitations applying *only* to general Warranty Claims.

**4. Fundamental / Title / Capacity**
- **Departure:** The Seller wants these under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Why it matters:** Title to 100% of the shares is the core of the deal. Capping title at 20% of price makes no commercial sense.
- **Push back:** Keep a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.

**5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to all Claims (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
- **Departure:** There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Why it matters:** This is a non-negotiable playbook position, and nobody on our side can waive it. As drafted, the Seller could rely on caps, time bars and non-reliance even for deliberate misstatement.
- **Push back:** Insert an express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct (by the Seller, its officers, agents or advisers) from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.

### B. Disclosure and Knowledge

**6. General disclosure (Schedule 7; DL 1.1–1.2)**
- **Departure:** Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" are all deemed disclosed.
- **Why it matters:** This would qualify every warranty by anything buried anywhere in the data room or any register.
- **Push back:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Disclosure should be limited to specific disclosures in the letter, made fairly and with enough detail for us to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Also:
  - Nothing is disclosed against Fundamental warranties, Tax covenant or specific indemnities.
  - DL 1.4 (non-admission) is acceptable only if it is made clear that it does not reduce any indemnity or the effect of a disclosure.
  - Any update to the disclosures before Completion requires our consent and does not cure a breach.

**7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)**
- **Departure:** This is a blanket exclusion covering the Buyer, its advisers, and anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Why it matters:** Combined with item 6, it would bar claims for every matter in the Disclosure Letter, including the open items the Seller admits are unresolved.
- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it should apply to *Seller* knowledge only, through named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.

### C. Deal-Specific Items

**8. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3; DL 2)**
- **Facts:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. Consent is required under clause 11.2, with conditions in 11.3. The Seller admits it has provided neither a final consent nor evidence the conditions are satisfied.
- **Departure:** The Seller offers reasonable endeavours, with the condition deemed satisfied as soon as it delivers Bluefen's written consent. Its claim that consent is "addressed" is contradicted by its own Disclosure Letter.
- **Push back:**
  - Make it a condition precedent: an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent, plus evidence before Completion that the 11.3 conditions are met.
  - Consent on delivery of a letter is not enough.
  - Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a customer of this size.
  - Only we can waive the condition.

**9. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DL 3)**
- **Facts:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with change-control at 8.1 and discharge at 9.2. The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is provided.
- **Departure:** The Seller offers a release "following Completion."
- **Why it matters:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release leaves security over the Company's assets (and possibly the shares) with a bank that has change-control rights.
- **Push back:** Require all of the following:
  - a current payout letter giving an exact figure and per diem (not "approximately");
  - repayment directly from Completion funds;
  - the payout counted as Debt in the price;
  - executed security releases and PPSR discharges delivered at Completion.

  A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable lender undertaking *and* Amelia Frost's approval. We do not have that approval.

**10. Funds flow and DD-005 bonuses (DL 5)**
- **Facts:** AUD 420k of conditional Completion bonuses are owed by the Company to its employees. The Seller confirms they are not in the funds flow. Payroll tax, super and other on-costs are unaddressed.
- **Departure:** Saying they are "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow means the Company, and therefore we, would bear them after Completion. "Agreed price mechanics" is not agreed.
- **Push back:** Show the AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, treated as Debt or Transaction Expenses, or as seller-funded. Back this with a specific indemnity for any shortfall. Ask for confirmation of the on-cost amounts.

**11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4)**
- **Facts:** Transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, but that is not bank-verified either way. There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Departure:** The Seller calls the indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, "adequate."
- **Push back:** Broaden the indemnity to cover:
  - failure of the Company to own or validly obtain Ironquay IP;
  - third-party or Ironquay claims;
  - costs of re-creating or licensing the materials;
  - consequential business loss.

  Keep the SOW3 cure as a pre-Completion deliverable: verified payment of all SOW3 fees and an executed confirmatory assignment. Do not assume the AUD 180k is owed or paid until it is verified. The indemnity should sit outside the general cap and thresholds.

**12. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6)**
- **Facts:** A download link went to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records may be involved. Access, scope and any notification duty are unknown, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Departure:** "Not expected to be material" is an unsupported Seller assertion.
- **Our position:** We should not accept that the matter is immaterial, and we should not assert it is a confirmed breach, attribute harm, assume a notification duty or put a number on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Seller covenants to preserve all logs and evidence.
  - Seller completes a proper investigation, with regular written updates and access for our advisers.
  - Any regulator or individual notification is made in consultation with us.
  - Ensure general disclosure and the knowledge bar do not extinguish claims arising from this matter.
  - Reserve our position on a specific indemnity until the facts are established.

**13. Sandbar renewals: AUD 330k (DL 8)**
- **Facts:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each, to be read together. The Disclosure Letter says nothing on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Departure:** The Seller's "ordinary-course" label is not supported by its own disclosure.
- **Push back:** Treat this as an assessment item, not an automatic Debt classification or price deduction. Request:
  - the contracts;
  - timing relative to Completion;
  - termination rights;
  - accrual status;
  - why the three are "related" (including any related-party angle).

  Then decide the treatment, whether ordinary course, a leakage-style concern or a conduct-of-business restriction.

**14. Tax and IP warranties**
- **Departure:** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are open, so they are not settled.
- **Push back:** Keep them as separate categories with their own regime, to be negotiated. We should not concede that the general cap, thresholds or timing apply. Equally, we should not assume unlimited liability has been agreed.

**15. Title evidence (DL 10)**
- **Facts:** The DD-012 share register is an internal document supplied by the Seller. The Seller itself notes we have not verified it.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence:
  - a current ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share certificates or an issuance history;
  - a PPSR search over the Seller and the shares;
  - confirmation of no options, convertibles or pre-emptive rights;
  - evidence of the Seller's corporate authority (board resolution, constitution);
  - releases of any Riverlark security over the shares.

  Using public searches to verify title is different from accepting them as deemed disclosure. We do the former and reject the latter.

**16. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- The Seller's characterisations (notification only for the lease; no consent needed for Mossvale) may well be right.
- We should confirm them ourselves on the underlying provisions rather than rely on the Disclosure Letter.
- Make the lease notification a Completion deliverable or covenant.

---

## 3. Summary of Recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / 4.8m | **25% / 6.0m.** Fallback not authorised. |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k excess | **5k / 50k tipping.** Not applicable to non-general claims. |
| 3 | Time limit | 18 months + all-claims override | **24 months.** Delete override; separate regimes. |
| 4 | Fundamental / Title | General regime | **100% cap, at least 6 years,** outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. |
| 5 | Limitations / non-reliance | All claims, no carve-out | **Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out.** Non-waivable. |
| 6 | Disclosure | Data room + registers | **Specific fair disclosure only.** Refresh from 22 Sept. |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket incl. advisers / discoverable | **Delete.** Named Seller knowledge persons only, if any. |
| 8 | Bluefen (~30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours, deemed on delivery | **CP:** effective consent + evidence 11.3 conditions met. |
| 9 | Riverlark (~3.2m) | Post-Completion release | **Payout letter, repay from Completion funds, releases at Completion.** |
| 10 | Bonuses 420k + on-costs | Excluded from funds flow | **Line item or seller-funded,** plus indemnity. |
| 11 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 indemnity | **Broaden;** keep SOW3 cure; verify the 180k. |
| 12 | DD-006 | "Not material" | **Preservation, investigation and update covenants;** no assumptions either way. |
| 13 | Sandbar 330k | Ordinary course | **Request information;** no automatic Debt treatment or deduction. |
| 14 | Tax / IP | "Settled" | **Open;** separate regimes. |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent ASIC / PPSR / authority evidence.** |

**Process recommendations**

1. **Hold our starting positions on every point.** None of the Seller's proposals has been cleared through our authority process. If the team later wants to use the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks, seek Amelia Frost's written approval identifying this specific draft. I would advise against it now: the overall package is heavily seller-skewed, and conceding headline numbers while the thresholds, the override and the fraud carve-out are unresolved would give away leverage.
2. **Lead the mark-up with the structural points:** fraud carve-out, deleting the all-claims override, separate Fundamental/Tax/IP regimes, disclosure and knowledge. These change the value of every other term.
3. **Send an information request** covering:
   - the Bluefen consent and evidence on the 11.3 conditions;
   - the Riverlark payout letter;
   - bonus on-costs;
   - Ironquay payment verification and a confirmatory assignment;
   - DD-006 investigation status and log preservation;
   - the Sandbar contracts;
   - independent title evidence;
   - a refreshed disclosure position (any changes since 22 September 2026).
4. **Respond to the cover note neutrally.** Note that we do not accept the Seller's characterisations ("negotiated," "addressed," "agreed," "settled," "adequate," "not material") as agreed positions.

  - Only we can waive the condition.

**9. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DL 3)**
- **Facts:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with change-control at 8.1 and discharge at 9.2. The facility has not been repaid and no discharge is provided.
- **Departure:** The Seller offers a release "following Completion."
- **Why it matters:** The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release leaves security over the Company's assets (and possibly the shares) with a bank that has change-control rights.
- **Push back:** Require all of the following:
  - a current payout letter giving an exact figure and per diem (not "approximately");
  - repayment directly from Completion funds;
  - the payout counted as Debt in the price;
  - executed security releases and PPSR discharges delivered at Completion.

  A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable lender undertaking *and* Amelia Frost's approval. We do not have that approval.

**10. Funds flow and DD-005 bonuses (DL 5)**
- **Facts:** AUD 420k of conditional Completion bonuses are owed by the Company to its employees. The Seller confirms they are not in the funds flow. Payroll tax, super and other on-costs are unaddressed.
- **Departure:** Saying they are "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow means the Company, and therefore we, would bear them after Completion. "Agreed price mechanics" is not agreed.
- **Push back:** Show the AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, treated as Debt or Transaction Expenses, or as seller-funded. Back this with a specific indemnity for any shortfall. Ask for confirmation of the on-cost amounts.

**11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4)**
- **Facts:** Transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, but that is not bank-verified either way. There is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Departure:** The Seller calls the indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, "adequate."
- **Push back:** Broaden the indemnity to cover:
  - failure of the Company to own or validly obtain Ironquay IP;
  - third-party or Ironquay claims;
  - costs of re-creating or licensing the materials;
  - consequential business loss.

  Keep the SOW3 cure as a pre-Completion deliverable: verified payment of all SOW3 fees and an executed confirmatory assignment. Do not assume the AUD 180k is owed or paid until it is verified. The indemnity should sit outside the general cap and thresholds.

**12. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6)**
- **Facts:** A download link went to an unintended external address. About 1,240 records may be involved. Access, scope and any notification duty are unknown, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Departure:** "Not expected to be material" is an unsupported Seller assertion.
- **Our position:** We should not accept that the matter is immaterial, and we should not assert it is a confirmed breach, attribute harm, assume a notification duty or put a number on it.
- **Push back:**
  - Seller covenants to preserve all logs and evidence.
  - Seller completes a proper investigation, with regular written updates and access for our advisers.
  - Any regulator or individual notification is made in consultation with us.
  - Ensure general disclosure and the knowledge bar do not extinguish claims arising from this matter.
  - Reserve our position on a specific indemnity until the facts are established.

**13. Sandbar renewals: AUD 330k (DL 8)**
- **Facts:** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each, to be read together. The Disclosure Letter says nothing on whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- **Departure:** The Seller's "ordinary-course" label is not supported by its own disclosure.
- **Push back:** Treat this as an assessment item, not an automatic Debt classification or price deduction. Request:
  - the contracts;
  - timing relative to Completion;
  - termination rights;
  - accrual status;
  - why the three are "related" (including any related-party angle).

  Then decide the treatment, whether ordinary course, a leakage-style concern or a conduct-of-business restriction.

**14. Tax and IP warranties**
- **Departure:** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are open, so they are not settled.
- **Push back:** Keep them as separate categories with their own regime, to be negotiated. We should not concede that the general cap, thresholds or timing apply. Equally, we should not assume unlimited liability has been agreed.

**15. Title evidence (DL 10)**
- **Facts:** The DD-012 share register is an internal document supplied by the Seller. The Seller itself notes we have not verified it.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence:
  - a current ASIC company extract consistent with the register;
  - share certificates or an issuance history;
  - a PPSR search over the Seller and the shares;
  - confirmation of no options, convertibles or pre-emptive rights;
  - evidence of the Seller's corporate authority (board resolution, constitution);
  - releases of any Riverlark security over the shares.

  Using public searches to verify title is different from accepting them as deemed disclosure. We do the former and reject the latter.

**16. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- The Seller's characterisations (notification only for the lease; no consent needed for Mossvale) may well be right.
- We should confirm them ourselves on the underlying provisions rather than rely on the Disclosure Letter.
- Make the lease notification a Completion deliverable or covenant.

| 3 | Time limit | 18 months + all-claims override | **24 months.** Delete override; separate regimes. |

**Process recommendations**

1. **Hold our starting positions on every point.** None of the Seller's proposals has been cleared through our authority process. If the team later wants to use the 20% cap or 18-month fallbacks, seek Amelia Frost's written approval identifying this specific draft. I would advise against it now: the overall package is heavily seller-skewed, and conceding headline numbers while the thresholds, the override and the fraud carve-out are unresolved would give away leverage.
2. **Lead the mark-up with the structural points:** fraud carve-out, deleting the all-claims override, separate Fundamental/Tax/IP regimes, disclosure and knowledge. These change the value of every other term.
3. **Send an information request** covering:
   - the Bluefen consent and evidence on the 11.3 conditions;
   - the Riverlark payout letter;
   - bonus on-costs;
   - Ironquay payment verification and a confirmatory assignment;
   - DD-006 investigation status and log preservation;
   - the Sandbar contracts;
   - independent title evidence;
   - a refreshed disclosure position (any changes since 22 September 2026).
4. **Respond to the cover note neutrally.** Note that we do not accept the Seller's characterisations ("negotiated," "addressed," "agreed," "settled," "adequate," "not material") as agreed positions.
